title: Finite-field scalar generator dévissage for all-continuous coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. On profinite sets put $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, using all continuous maps, and, for each finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$, put $A_E(P)=C(P,E)$ with the restricted norm topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $Y$ put $B_Y=p_Y^*B$ and $A_{E,Y}=p_Y^*A_E$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The map $A_{E,Y}\to B_Y$ is induced by postcomposition with $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and derived scalar extension $B_Y\otimes^L_{A_{E,Y}}-$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. A module is constructible when it has finite constant local models on a finite constructible locally closed scheme stratification [sk-def-sfb-constructible, det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model, def-constructible-stratification]; $\mathcal B_E(Y)$ and $\mathcal B_B(Y)$ denote complexes with bounded constructible cohomology for $A_E$ and $B$, respectively.

Let $a:S\hookrightarrow T$ be a constructible locally closed $k$-immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $L$ be a lisse $B_S$-module, meaning finite free on a pro-etale cover [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. For each locally closed immersion $c$, use exact extension $c_!=i_*v_!$ for an open-then-closed factorization, and apply it termwise to complexes [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. There exist a finite partition $S=\coprod_{t=1}^n V_t$ by constructible locally closed subschemes, with immersions $b_t:V_t\hookrightarrow S$, finite intermediate fields $E_t$, and lisse $A_{E_t,V_t}$-modules $N_t$, with the following properties. There is an ordinary coefficient-extension isomorphism $L|_{V_t}\cong B_{V_t}\otimes_{A_{E_t,V_t}}N_t$ for each $t$. The complexes
$$C_t=(a_!b_{t,!}N_t)[0]\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_{E_t,T}})$$
belong to $\mathcal B_{E_t}(T)$, and there are isomorphisms in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_T})$
$$B_T\otimes^L_{A_{E_t,T}}C_t\ \cong\ G_t:=\bigl(a_!b_{t,!}(B_{V_t}\otimes_{A_{E_t,V_t}}N_t)\bigr)[0].$$
These are the canonical support projection comparisons and respect the $B_T$-actions. There exist objects $F_0=0,F_1,\ldots,F_n\cong(a_!L)[0]$ and distinguished triangles $F_{t-1}\to F_t\to G_t\to F_{t-1}[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The partition can be chosen good: the closure of each stratum is a union of strata. If $S$ is empty the filtration and partition are empty. Rank-zero local systems are included; fields $E_t$ need not be equal.

source.place: Paragraph (3), all-continuous open-image argument; extraction of returned lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-open-finiteness steps 2--3 (good refinement, localization filtration, finite-field supported complexes and B-linear derived support projection). Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Lemma 3.4 supplies the generic exact immersion-extension context.

proof.text: The schemes $S,T$ are Noetherian: apply finite-type preservation of Noetherianity to their structure morphisms, since a field has only the ideals $0,k$. The minimal-closed-subset property gives the descending-chain condition on their closed subsets, and every subset is quasi-compact. In particular every open immersion in the argument has retrocompact image. If $S$ is empty choose $n=0$; extension from the empty site is zero and the assertions follow. Otherwise $L$ is constructible: a finite free local model is $B\otimes_{\underline\Omega}\underline{\Omega^r}$, a finite constant local model, and the one-stratum partition suffices. Apply stratified finite models to obtain a finite scheme partition $S=\coprod_a S_a$, fields $E_a$, lisse modules $N_a$ and ordinary $B_{S_a}$-linear isomorphisms $B_{S_a}\otimes_{A_{E_a,S_a}}N_a\cong L|_{S_a}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), source finite-field models; finite free local models as in HRS Definition 3.5.

proof.text: Apply good refinement to the underlying finite locally closed partition $|S|=\coprod_a|S_a|$, obtaining nonempty locally closed parts $Q_t$, each contained in some $|S_{a(t)}|$. Order the parts by repeatedly removing a maximal member for the relation $Q_u\preceq Q_v$ if $Q_u\subseteq\overline{Q_v}$. Antisymmetry follows since a locally closed subset is open dense in its closure: two disjoint parts cannot both be open dense in the same closure. In this ordering each initial union $U_t=\bigcup_{s\le t}Q_s$ is open: its complement is a downward closed set of parts and is the finite union of their closures. Thus $U_0=\varnothing$ and $U_n=S$. Give $U_t$ its open scheme structure and $Q_t=U_t\setminus U_{t-1}$ the reduced induced closed structure $z_t:V_t\hookrightarrow U_t$. Put $b_t=u_tz_t$ with $u_t:U_t\hookrightarrow S$. This also gives the reduced locally closed structure on $Q_t$, with good underlying partition.

source.place: Tag 09Y5, lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification; definition-good-stratification (09Y0); schemes.tex Tag 01J3 for the reduced closed structure.

proof.text: There is an actual scheme morphism $h_t:V_t\to S_{a(t)}$ over $S$. Indeed restrict $S_{a(t)}\hookrightarrow S$ to an open neighborhood in which it is closed. The image containment puts $V_t$ inside that open neighborhood, and the reduced-source factorization criterion applies to the resulting closed immersion. Set $E_t=E_{a(t)}$ and $N_t=h_t^*N_{a(t)}$. A base-changed trivializing pro-etale cover trivializes $N_t$: inverse image sends a finite free regular module to the finite free regular module of the same rank. Pull the chosen scalar-model isomorphism back along $h_t$. The ordinary balanced scalar/inverse-image comparison and the pullback compositor identify its two sides with $B_{V_t}\otimes_{A_{E_t,V_t}}N_t$ and $L|_{V_t}$. This gives the required ordinary coefficient-linear model. No factorization through a nonreduced subscheme is inferred from image containment without the reduced-source criterion. The internal/sectionwise scalar-adjunction comparison identifies these balanced tensor maps with the internal scalar extensions, including their destination-ring actions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), refinement of source finite-field models; Stacks Tag 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction) and sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback).

proof.text: First $c_t=ab_t$ is an immersion, as can be checked without assuming that image containment alone suffices. Factor $a$ as $S\hookrightarrow O\hookrightarrow T$, closed then open. The open $U_t\subset S$ is $S\cap W_t$ for an open $W_t\subset O$. Hence $U_t\hookrightarrow W_t$ is closed, and its composite with the closed $V_t\hookrightarrow U_t$ is closed by composition of closed immersions. Thus $c_t$ is closed into the open $W_t$ of $T$. For each $t$ put $c_t=ab_t$. The exact locally closed extension comparisons identify $a_!b_{t,!}N_t\cong c_{t,!}N_t$ and likewise for the ordinary $B$-scalar extension of $N_t$. All these identifications restrict to the identity on $V_t$. Apply the lisse-extension constructibility statement with the finite field $E_t$, ambient Noetherian scheme $T$, support $c_t$, and lisse module $N_t$. It gives $(c_{t,!}N_t)[0]\in\mathcal B_{E_t}(T)$; the preceding comparison gives the asserted membership of $C_t$. Only the finite-field clause is used, so no convention on the topology of the algebraic closure is imported here.

source.place: Lemma 3.4, exact support extension; finite-field finite-constant-model formulation in the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Apply the unbounded support/scalar comparison to $A_{E_t}\to B$ and $c_t$, with input $N_t[0]$. It gives $B_T\otimes^L_{A_{E_t,T}}(c_{t,!}N_t)[0]\cong c_{t,!}(B_{V_t}\otimes^L_{A_{E_t,V_t}}N_t[0])$. The lisse-input clause identifies the inner derived scalar extension with $(B_{V_t}\otimes_{A_{E_t,V_t}}N_t)[0]$. Using Step 4 on both sides proves the displayed comparison $B_T\otimes^L C_t\cong G_t$. For its specified normalization, use supported common-field scalar models with both supports $c_t$, both fields $E_t$, and both local systems $N_t$. Then $E_tE_t=E_t$ and multiplication identifies the preliminary regular scalar extension with $N_t$. Its destination-$B$ comparison, after scalar reassociation, is exactly this support comparison: it is the open identity under the open unit and the scalar-pullback/closed-counit comparison at the closed factor. Thus the comparison is the canonical one, linear over $B_T$; normalization does not follow merely from an abstract isomorphism of underlying abelian objects.

source.place: Paragraph (3), derived coefficient/support projection; normalized all-continuous support comparisons stated in the cited existing nodes.

proof.text: Define $M_t=u_{t,!}(L|_{U_t})$ on $S$. In $U_t$, apply module open-closed localization to the open $U_{t-1}$ and the reduced closed complement $z_t:V_t\hookrightarrow U_t$. Its hypotheses hold by Noetherianity and quasi-compactness from Step 1. It gives $0\to j_!(L|_{U_{t-1}})\to L|_{U_t}\to z_{t,*}(L|_{V_t})\to0$. Exact $u_{t,!}$ and normalized composition of immersion extensions give $0\to M_{t-1}\to M_t\to b_{t,!}(L|_{V_t})\to0$. The arrows into $L$ are the open counits; localization makes them monomorphisms and their composites agree by the adjunction composition laws. Here $M_0=0$ and $M_n=L$. Applying exact $a_!$ yields $0\to a_!M_{t-1}\to a_!M_t\to a_!b_{t,!}(L|_{V_t})\to0$.

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; Tag 09BM, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact.

proof.text: Put $F_t=(a_!M_t)[0]$. The short exact sequence of Step 6, regarded as a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes concentrated in degree zero, gives a distinguished triangle. Its third object is $G_t$ by the ordinary model isomorphism of Step 3. Thus $F_{t-1}\to F_t\to G_t\to F_{t-1}[1]$ is distinguished, $F_0=0$, and $F_n\cong(a_!L)[0]$. The chosen partition is good by Step 2. For a rank-zero restriction choose its finite-field model to be zero at the model-selection step; the corresponding triangle is permitted to have zero third object; no step assumed positive rank or strictness of the filtration. The fields are indexed separately throughout, so no common field assertion is needed.

(2) The order Q_u ⪯ Q_v ⇔ Q_u ⊆ cl(Q_v) is antisymmetric because two dense opens of the same closure meet; maximal-first removal plus goodness makes the initial unions open (checked by hand); V_t gets the reduced structure (01J3). Locally-closed-extension-coherence identifies a_!b_! with c_! and with the closure factorization, and the heart-lisse-extension lemma is applied with Λ=E_t on T. (5) finite-stage-supported-generation gives the R'-linear support comparison and degree-zero concentration; supported-common-field-scalar-models with E=F=E_t and a=b=c_t gives the normalization (both nodes unsplit and more general, not clause restatements). (7) complex-ses-triangle gives the triangles; the third term is identified with G_t via the Step 3 model.
